summary: Tetsuro Watsuji worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, under Natsume Sōseki, and Martin Heidegger. He held posts at Keio, Tsuda, Hosei, Kyoto University (1925, 1931–1934), and Tokyo (1934–1949).

Tetsuzo Tanikawa was a philosopher who studied at the First Higher School and Kyoto University. He held academic posts at Doshisha University and served as a professor at Hosei University from approximately 1938 to 1965.
Teun Goudriaan worked in Indology and religious studies. He was affiliated with Utrecht University, where he held a post attested in 1989 and was attested as Professor Emeritus in 2000.

Thanissaro Bhikkhu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oberlin College and trained under Ajahn Fuang Jotiko from circa 1976 to 1986. He founded Metta Forest Monastery and became its abbot in 1993.

Thegchog Dorje was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Pema Nyinje Wangpo and Kunzik Chokyi Nangwa, and he taught numerous disciples, including Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Chokgyur Lingpa.

Theodor Aufrecht was an Indologist and linguist who earned his dissertation at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Berlin (1850), the Bodleian Library (1852), the University of Edinburgh (1861–1875), and the University of Bonn (1875–1889).

Theodor Benfey worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Göttingen, completing his Ph.D. and habilitation, and at the University of Munich. He held teaching posts at Göttingen from 1834, becoming ordinarius from 1862 to 1881.

Theodor Bloch was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and history and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig University under Ernst Windisch from approximately 1888 to 1892, and later studied under Georg Bühler between 1892 and 1895.

Theodor Goldstücker was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Königsberg and Bonn, as well as under Peter von Bohlen, Karl Rosenkranz, Christian Lassen, and Eugène Burnouf. He was a Sanskrit professor at the University of London from 1851 to 1872.

Theodor Nöldeke worked in linguistics, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Göttingen under Heinrich Ewald and Theodor Benfey, he held posts at Göttingen, Kiel University (1864, 1868), and the University of Strasbourg (1872–1906).

Theodor Zachariae was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig and Göttingen under Georg Curtius, Hermann Brockhaus, Hermann Sauppe, and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at the University of Greifswald (1883) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1890–1921).

Theodore Dwight Woolsey worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He was educated at Yale and Princeton, later serving as president of Yale University from 1831 to 1871 and president of the American Oriental Society from 1870 to 1882.

Theodore Gabriel is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He earned an M.Litt from the University of Aberdeen and served as a Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Gloucestershire.
Theodorus Willem Juynboll was a religious studies scholar who studied at Leiden University between approximately 1885 and 1893. He held a post at Utrecht University in 1916.
Theophil Gubler was an Indologist and linguist who completed his doctoral degree at the University of Basel in 1903, having studied under Jacob Wackernagel.

Thich Nhat Hanh was a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. He studied at Saigon, Princeton, and Columbia. He held posts at Columbia, Princeton, Vạn Hạnh University, and Cornell, and studied under Thanh Quý Chân Thật.
Thich Thien Nghiem is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Delhi, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Shalini Singhal, attested in 2012.
Thierry Mathou is a scholar in Tibetology who studied at EDHEC Business School and Sciences Po. He has served as an Associated Political Scientist at the CNRS.

Thierry Meynard is a scholar in sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned a PhD at Peking University under Yulie Lou. He became Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University around 2006 and directed The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies in 2012.

Thinh Canh Quang is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of the West, attested in 2007, studying under Lewis Lancaster, Ananda Guruge, and doctoral supervisor Kottegoda Warnasuriya.
